questions.q: What is the reactivity series of metals?
a: A list of metals arranged in order of their chemical reactivity from most reactive to least reactive
A table showing the melting points of rocks
A list of non-metals grouped by color

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a very reactive metal that bubbles vigorously and catches fire in water?
How do unreactive metals like gold and platinum typically occur in the Earth's crust?
a: As metal oxides mixed with soil
As soluble salts dissolved in oceans
As uncombined native elements in pure form

questions.q: What happens when a more reactive metal is placed into a solution of a less reactive metal salt?
a: The metals fuse into an alloy
A displacement reaction occurs, where the more reactive metal displaces the less reactive metal from its solution

questions.q: What gas is typically produced when a reactive metal like magnesium or zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
Which of the following metals is *not* reactive enough to displace hydrogen from dilute acids?
If you put a piece of copper metal into a solution of zinc sulfate, what observation would you make?
a: No reaction occurs because copper is less reactive than zinc

questions.q: What is observed when a clean piece of magnesium ribbon is dropped into copper(II) sulfate solution?
a: The magnesium shrinks and disappears with no other change
The blue color fades and brown/pink copper metal coats the magnesium

questions.q: Which of the following metals is the most reactive among standard common laboratory metals?
Why is aluminum considered reasonably reactive chemically, yet objects made of aluminum do not corrode away quickly in air?
a: It is protected by a thin, tough, unreactive layer of aluminum oxide on its surface
It reacts with nitrogen to form a shield
It is actually less reactive than gold

questions.q: How can very unreactive metals like iron oxide be extracted from their ores in industry?
a: By heating the metal oxide with carbon in a blast furnace

questions.q: How are very reactive metals (like potassium, sodium, and calcium) extracted from their compounds?
a: By electrolysis of molten metal compounds

questions.q: Which metal reacts vigorously with cold water to form a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas?
Which metal reacts slowly with cold water, but reacts readily with steam to form an oxide and hydrogen?
What is formed when a metal burns in oxygen gas?
If iron nail is placed in a solution of copper sulfate, what happens to the color of the solution over time?
a: The blue color fades as copper is displaced and iron enters solution

questions.q: Which metal is positioned just above hydrogen in the reactivity series, meaning it reacts with acids but not with cold water?
What term describes the gradual destruction or eating away of metals due to chemical reactions with oxygen, moisture, or acids in the environment?
Why is iron used widely for building construction rather than sodium or potassium?
a: Sodium and potassium are too heavy
Sodium and potassium are extremely reactive and dangerous to handle in air or water
Iron is more reactive than sodium

questions.q: What substance is essential for iron to rust, in addition to oxygen?
Which of the following metals is often used to coat steel pipes or sheets to prevent rusting through a process called galvanizing?
What is the primary chemical name for rust?
If metal X displaces metal Y from a solution of its salt, what can you deduce about their positions in the reactivity series?
a: Metal X is less reactive than metal Y
Metal X and Y have identical reactivity
Metal X is higher (more reactive) than metal Y

questions.q: Which of the following methods will *not* prevent iron from rusting?
a: Connecting it to a sacrificial anode
Placing it in pure dry oxygen with no water

questions.q: What is observed when calcium metal is added to cold water?
a: Fizzing/bubbling of hydrogen gas, a white precipitate of calcium hydroxide forming, and the metal moving around
The water turns bright pink permanently

questions.q: Why are precious metals like gold and silver traditionally used for making jewelry and coins?
a: They are unreactive, do not corrode, and maintain their shiny appearance
They are the most reactive metals known

questions.q: In a displacement reaction between zinc and copper(II) sulfate, which substance is oxidized or loses electrons?
Which metal would be able to reduce copper oxide to copper metal when heated together?
What happens when iron filings are added to a solution of silver nitrate?
a: Iron displaces silver, forming silver crystals on the iron and turning the solution green with iron nitrate

questions.q: Which of the following lists places the four metals in correct order from most reactive to least reactive?
What is 'sacrificial protection' in the context of preventing iron from rusting?
a: Attaching a more reactive metal (like zinc or magnesium) that corrodes in place of the iron

questions.q: Why does a piece of copper pipe not react when left outside in the rain for years?
a: Rainwater has no effect on metals
Copper is located below hydrogen in the reactivity series and does not react with dilute acids or water

questions.q: Which of the following metals will react most violently with dilute hydrochloric acid?
What is the chemical purpose of adding carbon (coke) into a blast furnace along with iron ore (iron oxide)?
a: To act as a reducing agent that removes oxygen from the iron oxide, leaving molten iron

Which of the following correctly pairs a metal with its correct extraction method based on reactivity?

a: Turns blue or purple because an alkaline metal hydroxide is formed
Turns bright red because a strong acid is formed

questions.q: Why can carbon be used to extract iron from iron ore, but cannot be used to extract aluminum from aluminum oxide?
a: Carbon is more reactive than iron, but less reactive than aluminum
Aluminum oxide does not contain oxygen

Which of the following statements about the reactivity series is scientifically accurate?
a: All metals react with water at the same speed
Non-metals are always placed at the top of the reactivity series
Metals at the bottom of the series form oxides very easily
